dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He doesn't seem to notice your approach. Still immersed in his own thoughts, he shakes his head and lets out a long sigh.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (This guy seems promising enough. Maybe I can get some information out of him!)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hello, sir! Is there anything I can do to help you?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Wait, you're...!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Erm, I'm...

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Oh, dear goodness, you're... you're a Marechaussee Hunter!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You recognize us? Ah, are you... one of the people who wrote the commission letter?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! I didn't expect you to actually come. What great news... The city is saved!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What happened here?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Alas... We once lived comfortable, carefree lives. This city used to be free of monsters. The first Marechaussee Hunter, Cassiodor, the "Golden Hunter," he was the one who drove them back.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: However... Monsters have once again surrounded the city. Perhaps the seal that kept them at bay has lost its power, or perhaps an evil sorcerer has been meddling in our affairs. All I know for sure is that their return has stripped this city of any chance at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Are there... not enough soldiers to drive them out?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: It's not a question of numbers. The guards simply have no idea how to deal with them.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Most people my age have never even seen one of the monsters, much less been trained to fight against them. What's worse, many of us don't even know the history of the Marechaussee Hunters anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: When I was a child, though, my grandfather would tell me stories about how the Marechaussee Hunters drove back the monsters. So, on the off-chance that something might come of it, I decided to reach out to you.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: To be perfectly honest, I was starting to think all those stories were just tall tales, but now that I've seen you in person, I finally know that it was true!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, you can rest easy, friend! The righteous and formidable Marechaussee Hunters are on the case!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The man is touched by your determination and resolve. His eyes begin to well with tears of relief.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Still, if we're going to hunt the monsters, we need to know where to find them. Can you give us any leads?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: All I know is that the area outside the city is dangerous. I'm afraid I can't point you toward a specific location.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Although, if you leave the capital through the main gate and follow the road, you should run into a group of guards. They might know more about where to find the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I see... We'll go look for them, then.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Alright, be careful. Oh and... one last thing. The monsters outside the city are just part of the problem. There are evil sorcerers inside the city as well, so be on your guard.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: They're actively working with the monsters, and have corrupted the court ministers with malicious magic. They're the reason why, even inside the city, everything has been a giant mess.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Even one of our kindest ministers has turned into a boorish and unreasonable figure, interested in nothing but enacting laws that exploit the people. Who knows how much longer we'll be able to go on like this...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Talk about being stuck between a rock and a hard place...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I feel bad for him. Maybe we should try to cheer him up?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hey, not everything can be solved with food!

response.speaker: Anxious Man
response.text: I appreciate your kindness, but for now, it's more important to focus on the crisis at hand.

response.speaker: Anxious Man
response.text: Brave Hunters, I leave the future of this kingdom to you.

choices.text: Furina could sing him a song?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh? Like... now? Is this really the right time...?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If I understood correctly, there are currently two problems in the kingdom that need solving, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Exactly. We need to defeat the monsters outside the city and take down the evil sorcerers stirring up trouble from within.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But, which problem should we tackle first...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, this seems like a good moment for a break. Take some time, and discuss what you want to do. Let me know when you've made your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh... I really didn't expect the people in the city to keep us at arm's length like that. I totally thought the Hunters would be treated like heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Clorinde said the script took cues from the real history of Fontaine, right? Maybe the real-life Marechaussee Hunters were also treated like that?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I wouldn't say it's a perfect representation of history, but there are definitely some similarities. Would you like to hear more about it?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sure, as long as it doesn't spoil anything in the script! You've brought up bits and pieces of the Hunters' history before, but it was all in passing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to know, too! The Hunters were super powerful, right? Were they all from a special line of supernatural beings or something? Kinda like... the youkai in Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: No, all Marechaussee Hunters were ordinary mortal fighters. The only thing that set them apart were the special sword techniques passed down over the centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So you mean... anyone could become a Marechaussee Hunter?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In theory, yes. All you would need to do is survive the rigorous training, and master the swordsmanship techniques required to fight the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Still, most people dropped out at the early stages, and others called it quits the minute they saw a monster in person. To become a Hunter, you must be strong in both body and mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of monsters did the Hunters fight exactly? Oh and, the "evil sorcerer" the script mentions — did they exist in real life, too?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The land of Fontaine once played host to an ancient dynasty known as Remuria. After that dynasty fell, monsters began to appear, intent on obstructing humans from establishing a new social order.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: One of the ancient sorcerers of Remuria used his power to assemble a formidable army of golems. He sought to use that force to establish himself as king.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now wait a second! Don't tell me that guy was the inspiration for the evil sorcerer in the script! We still haven't found any in-game information on him yet, so why don't you talk about someone else for now?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, I wasn't planning on going into anything you might be able to find out in the game... But, if you want me to talk about something else, then... How about Cassiodor, the Golden Hunter, or Egeria, the ex-Hydro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but those people are all from a super long time ago! Where did you learn all this, Clorinde?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: From my master.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: By "master," you mean... Ms. Petronilla?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Someone you know?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Absolutely. Ms. Petronilla and my father were good friends. Back in the day, she would often bring Clorinde over to play. But then...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...Let's not get off topic. Anyway, back to what I was saying...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Responding to Egeria's call, a number of warriors followed Cassiodor into battle against the monsters. This group of warriors, under Cassiodor's leadership, became known as the Marechaussee Hunters.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yet, as Fontaine entered an era of peace, their work gradually became obsolete. The Marechaussee Phantom, originally an association made up of Hunters, eventually came to be predominantly comprised of Melusines.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, I see... That explains why most of the people in the script have forgotten the Hunters or think of them as nothing more than a legend.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Is that really a bad thing, though? It can get tough always being the one shouldering everyone's expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm, depends on who you ask, I suppose. If the name of the organization no longer commands respect, investigative work is bound to suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Speaking of investigations, which problem should we tackle first? Monsters, or evil sorcerer?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I vote monsters. That's the main duty of the Hunters, right? We can come back to the sorcerer later.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well said, Miss Furina. Plus, if the sorcerer really are the masterminds behind this whole thing, defeating the monsters could give us some clues on their intentions as well.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What about you, partner? What do you think?

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Alright, after some discussion, you decide to turn around and head out of the city...

choices.text: The sorcerer problem seems pretty important...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I mean... you're not wrong. But, those characters are usually the ones pulling the strings behind the scenes. More often than not, they're very formidable opponents. Going after them now might be jumping the gun a little bit.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We don't want a total party kill on the first day, right? With Clorinde as the GM, I wouldn't rule out the possibility...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, then it's settled! Let's go hunt some monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The monsters let out a terrifying roar of anger and resentment, before dissipating into thin air.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Phew... Thank goodness it's over!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We're lucky the Marechaussee Hunter class came with all those preset skill points. Otherwise, we would've been in some real trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I never knew the Fateometer even determines the amount of damage you inflict... If you get unlucky, isn't it just game over right then and there?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's part of the fun! The uncertainty of fate is what gives these games their appeal.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Just as you begin to celebrate your victory, a suspicious lump on the ground catches your attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A suspicious... lump? Wait, could it be... the thing that appears after every battle...!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I walk up to it, crouch down, and begin to carefully examine it. I've still got my right glove on, so it should be fine for me to touch it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you investigate the mound, you discover that the exposed portion appears to be made of wood. It was previously obscured by the large form of the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: With the monsters gone, the small protrusion now awaits your discovery, poking out of the ground like a shy flower bud.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah! It's a treasure chest!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's dig it up!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Looks like everyone's here. Before we begin, why don't we finish where we left off yesterday? There was an important decision to be made, yes? I'll pour everyone a cup of tea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I—Is that really the most important part, though, Clorinde? Paimon's more concerned about our current surroundings...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heavy walls, cold railings, dim lights... This is obviously supposed to be a prison!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I admire the work put into the set. Still, it's obvious the script writer has never paid a visit to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So this set... is going to be a part of the script?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, that is something I can neither confirm nor deny.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, anyone think Clorinde's smile is starting to look kinda scary...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, whatever happens, we'll just have to push on. But first, we should really figure out what to do with this treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If we're worried about arousing suspicion because of our identity... Why don't we give ourselves a different name, just like Clorinde's Master did?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yeah, it might be better to keep a low profile. As long as we're helping people, it doesn't matter who we are or what we're called.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Staring at me won't get you anywhere. Or, did you want some more tea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, um... Paimon's good! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why aren't you saying anything, Navia? Wait... What's that next to you?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, this is the short sword Clorinde mentioned last night. I found it!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Huh, I'm surprised you managed to track it down after all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, I made sure to take good care of it! Considering the... circumstances in which you gave it to me, of course I had to keep it safe.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, where were we? Oh, right, I was just thinking about all the potential ways for us to break out of prison! We could dig a tunnel, or try to bribe the guards...?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Wait, we haven't been thrown into prison yet, have we?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, it's only a matter of time! It pays to be prepared, just like how you should always have an umbrella on hand, even when it's sunny.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Paimon's made up her mind. Let's just give the treasure away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon may have wanted to keep it, but if that's going to land us in prison somehow, Paimon will be too upset to enjoy her snacks.

choices.text: Turns out Paimon cares more about snacks than treasure.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: So, you've reached an agreement? Alright then, we can continue with the story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and we'll collect all the scattered pieces of treasure on the ground as well!

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: You collect the treasure and make your way back to the capital with your bag of loot in hand.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The city is still shrouded in a gloomy, oppressive atmosphere, but your spirits are surprisingly high.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: In places where sunlight struggles to reach, you generously share your wealth with the children, the elderly, and the poor in urgent need of help.

dialogues.speaker: Hunchbacked Old Lady
dialogues.text: Thank you, kind soul...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The elderly woman's look of gratitude follows you as you walk away, her eyes never leaving your back until you move entirely out of sight. However, there's still quite a bit of Mora remaining. It appears you haven't made much progress.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (She's probably trying to tell us to speed this up. We need to hurry up so we can address the sorcerer problem...)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Should we go find that man again at the square? He seemed like a pretty responsible guy. I'm sure he knows the people here far better than us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good idea!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Just as you start to make way to the square, intent on finding the man again, there's a voice...

dialogues.speaker: Serious Guard
dialogues.text: Please wait, distinguished guests.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Several strange guards suddenly call out to you. They run forward to meet you and proceed to politely pay their respects.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Greetings, gentlemen! Are we being invited for afternoon tea?

dialogues.speaker: Serious Guard
dialogues.text: Surely, you jest, my lady. That would not be our place. It is His Excellency the king, who requests to meet with you. Please come with us.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you approach the battlefield, you see numerous people lying by the side of the road. They appear to be dressed like guards.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Their faces are filled with desperation and terror. Some are screaming and cursing in vain, as if still trying to banish the monstrosities they saw from their minds.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The next battle round begins... now.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Found something here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'd like to try to hit him with my sword.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Your strike is successful.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hah, you're facing a veteran Marechaussee Hunter. You don't stand a chance!

dialogues.speaker: "Guard"?
dialogues.text: Tch...
